jobs.title: RevOps Manager
jobs.description:
About Dreamdata

Dreamdata helps B2B marketing teams see which of their campaigns actually lead to revenue, by joining up the touchpoints a buying committee leaves across ads, web visits and the CRM.

Customers keep telling us it helps. Revenue has grown quickly for several years in a row, and new funding lets us open more markets.

To keep up, we want a hands-on RevOps Manager who will make our revenue tooling dependable for Sales, Marketing, SDR and Customer Success alike.

The Opportunity

This is a practical Revenue Operations job with a technical bent: system design, automation and integrations. You will look after the core go-to-market tools and the workflows that connect them. If you enjoy using AI to build and extend internal tooling, you will have room to shape how our internal platform grows.

You'll report to the COO and take day-to-day direction from the Senior Revenue Operations Manager. You will work with Marketing, Sales and Customer Success to keep our systems tidy, automated and trustworthy as we grow.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run HubSpot: objects, properties, lifecycle stages, workflows, permissions and routing
  • Build and look after Zapier/n8n automations, with retries, alerts and monitoring
  • Set up lead routing and round-robin rules by segment, region and SLA
  • Back the SDR team's outbound work with sound tooling and automation
  • Keep data clean across our tools (deduplication, enrichment, validation)
  • Watch the integrations between our tools and fix sync problems quickly
  • Work with RevOps, Sales, Marketing, Finance and CS to turn their needs into systems that scale

Requirements

Must-Have  

  • A record of automating go-to-market processes so that Sales, Marketing, SDR and Customer Success do less by hand
  • Hands-on HubSpot Admin experience (workflows, objects, lifecycle, routing)
  • Deep experience with Zapier or a similar tool, including long multi-step automations
  • You have built and maintained web forms and demo request flows
  • A clear grasp of lead routing, round-robin rules and handoffs between teams
  • At ease working side by side with commercial colleagues
  • Careful, proactive and keen to own systems from end to end
  • SQL or a similar language for pulling and analysing data from our systems

Nice-to-Have

  • SDR tooling (e.g. Outreach, Orum)
  • Enrichment tools (e.g. Apollo, ZoomInfo, Lusha)
  • Reverse ETL (Hightouch)
  • Product or web analytics (Segment)
  • BigQuery and Looker
  • Some exposure to software development
  • Some exposure to finance operations

Location

  • New York, NY
  • Occasional trips to our Copenhagen office

Benefits

Your work here will show up in the numbers quickly, and you will grow your skills alongside a team that likes to share what it knows.

We want a workplace where people of every background do their best work. If building reliable revenue systems sounds like your kind of job, we would like to hear from you.

  • Total Compensation: ~$145k for the right candidate
  • Health/Dental/Vision Insurance 100% Covered
  • 401(k)
  • Commuter Benefits
  • Office dogs

jobs.title: Staff Insights Engineer
jobs.description:
About Dreamdata

Dreamdata helps B2B marketing teams see which of their campaigns actually lead to revenue — joining up the touchpoints a buying committee leaves across ads, web visits and the CRM.

The company was started in 2018 by product and engineering people who had wanted such a tool in their earlier jobs and decided to build it themselves.

Customers keep telling us it helps. Revenue has grown quickly for several years, and new funding lets us open more markets.

We are growing the team and looking for experienced people who want to help shape the product.

 

The Opportunity

Our customers use the Dreamdata Platform to understand where their pipeline comes from. Put together, that gives us an unusually wide view of how companies buy software and services.

We turn that view into benchmark reports that marketers read and quote. We want those benchmarks to be the figures people trust when they ask how B2B marketing performs.

We are hiring a Staff Insights Engineer to build the data foundation behind them. This is a technical role at heart: analytics engineering, data science, and warehouse ownership make up most of the work.

Before we publish a number, someone has to model the dataset, aggregate and anonymise it properly, check that the method stands up, and build tools that let us answer new questions within hours. That someone is you. A benchmark is only as good as the data under it.

You will have help. Our marketing team plans the reports, writes the story and owns the brand. You own everything upstream of that, working closely with them: they tell you which questions matter, and you make sure the answers are right, quick and honestly qualified.

 

You own

  • The self-service layer and internal tools marketing uses
  • The warehouse models, pipelines and tests behind each published figure
  • Aggregation, anonymisation and minimum group sizes
  • Statistical method, and the caveats that go with each number
  • Getting the sample, denominator and scale right
  • Technical approval of anything we publish

Marketing owns, you support

  • Publishing calendar, cadence and channels
  • Headlines, story and visual finish
  • Our social channels and brand voice
  • Contact with press, newsletters and analysts
  • Report launches and events
  • Demand generation goals

Success means a data foundation that is correct, quick and trusted, and a marketing team that rarely waits on you.

The role sits in engineering, works daily with marketing, and takes on more ownership over time. Few jobs put deep warehouse work in front of a whole industry; this one does.

 

Key Responsibilities

First six months: lay the foundation

  • Learn our data model in depth alongside the engineering team, and model the benchmark dataset on it.
  • Strengthen the aggregation and anonymisation layer.
  • Put transformations on a proper footing: versioned models, tests, CI and documentation.
  • Write the metric definitions and semantic layer marketing can query on its own.
  • Set the bar for method: sample sizes, confidence intervals, and how we handle and disclose the fact that our data covers our own customers, not the whole market.

After that — keep it fast

  • Turn a good question into a sound answer quickly, and keep shortening that loop. Today marketing waits for engineering to run queries; you will end that wait for good.
  • Own the analysis for the quarterly benchmarks and the regular figures marketing publishes.
  • Review claims technically so we never say more than the data shows.
  • Keep self-service good enough that marketing answers most questions without you.

Requirements

Must have

  • Strong production SQL. Window functions, incremental models and tuning queries over large event tables. You write the queries yourself and think about cost as well as correctness.
  • Owned a warehouse. You have run a warehouse project from start to finish: dimensional or semantic modelling, a framework such as Dataform or dbt with tests, docs and CI, orchestration, and the habits that keep it healthy. We use BigQuery on Google Cloud.
  • Solid statistics. Sampling, confidence intervals, significance, cohort and survival analysis. You can tell noise from signal and know how a single vendor's customer base skews a benchmark.
  • Care with privacy. You have shared findings drawn from customer data under anonymisation and minimum-group rules you could defend to a security reviewer. We will not bend on this.
  • Plain technical writing. You can write a method note a marketer follows and an analyst cannot fault, and say clearly what a figure does and does not mean.
  • Correct charts. You make charts with the right cut, denominator and honest axes, then hand them to design for finish. You are not expected to be a designer or to write the copy.
  • Interest in how B2B buying works. You want to know what the data says. We can teach the domain, not the curiosity.
  • Independence, and ease with AI tools. You plan your own work and use tools like Claude and Cursor to move faster.

Nice to have

  • BigQuery and Google Cloud in particular.
  • dbt at scale, or another transformation framework you ran in production.
  • You were the analyst behind a published benchmark or data report.
  • Python for analysis: pandas, notebooks, and charts in matplotlib, Plotly, Vega or Tableau.
  • Background in B2B martech or RevOps: attribution, CDPs, ABM, growth analytics.
  • Opinions on B2B SaaS, go-to-market and how buyers behave.
  • Happy to speak about method on a podcast, at a conference or with an analyst. Welcome, never required.
  • A wish to publish some of your own work next to what marketing puts out.

Benefits

  • Location: An office in central Copenhagen by the water
  • Ownership: Shares in a growing company
  • Lunch: Lunch served in our canteen
  • Inclusive Culture: A friendly team that helps each other
  • Private insurance: Health insurance as part of our pension plan
  • Office dogs

Your work here will show up in public quickly, and you will grow your skills alongside a team that likes to share what it knows.

We want a workplace where people of every background do their best work. If you build data you would put your name to, and want it seen widely, we would like to hear from you.
